title: This Time with Feeling
coreMove: Turn repeated emotional load into explicit decision hygiene before fatigue distorts the call.
sourcePressure: The next hard decision arrives before recovery; experience sharpens pattern recognition but also adds memory, fatigue, hesitation, and numbness risk.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version is about being emotionally balanced or stoic under repeat stress.

hook: you cannot pour from an empty cup
counterintuition: experience does not make it easier

exampleSpecs.domain: wildfire incident command after a second wind shift
exampleSpecs.audience: an incident commander whose crew just contained one line and must choose a new evacuation zone
exampleSpecs.stakes: fatigue makes underreaction tempting while homes sit in the changed path
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the commander writes tradeoff, owner, consequence, and review time on the incident log before moving the evacuation boundary
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a wind map curling at the edges on the hood of a command truck

exampleSpecs.domain: airport baggage system recovery after two failures in one holiday week
exampleSpecs.audience: an airport operations chief deciding whether to keep manual sorting overnight
exampleSpecs.stakes: manual sorting protects departures but exhausts crews and hides the system fault
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the chief refuses to call the first fix proof, assigns one owner for overnight manual sorting, and sets a dawn trigger for shutting lanes again
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a conveyor belt stopped under a row of unclaimed red-tagged bags

exampleSpecs.domain: neonatal ICU staffing after a flu outbreak and a resignation
exampleSpecs.audience: a nurse director managing repeat shortage calls
exampleSpecs.stakes: overusing the same nurses may preserve the schedule while increasing patient risk
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the director marks which memory from last week's save is helping and which is pushing her toward numb acceptance of unsafe ratios
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a staffing grid with two names circled in thick black pen

exampleSpecs.domain: film post-production house after a second corrupted render
exampleSpecs.audience: a post supervisor with a festival deadline and a tired editing team
exampleSpecs.stakes: rushing another export may miss the real fault and ruin delivery
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the supervisor asks the team to predict the failure source, then requires a fresh owner and check step before another overnight render begins
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a failed render log frozen at 97 percent on a dark edit suite monitor

exampleSpecs.domain: city water lab after a second contamination alert
exampleSpecs.audience: a lab manager balancing public warning, retest protocol, and staff exhaustion
exampleSpecs.stakes: a false calm risks public health; a panic alert damages trust
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the manager has the lead tech state the tradeoff aloud, assigns the retest owner, and sets the public update threshold before samples leave the bench
exampleSpecs.firstImage: sample vials lined beside a laminated boil-water threshold card

exampleSpecs.domain: boutique hotel after a second weekend reservation-system outage
exampleSpecs.audience: a general manager deciding whether to comp rooms, close bookings, or keep improvising
exampleSpecs.stakes: front-desk staff are making inconsistent promises to guests
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the manager replaces ad hoc apologies with a written decision grid and a noon review signal for reopening bookings
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a lobby printer spitting duplicate reservation slips onto the floor

skillTargets: spot recurring strain versus isolated crisis
evaluate whether past experience is informing or distorting the next call

tryThisNowSpec: Before your next repeated hard call, write four words on the page: tradeoff, owner, consequence, review. Fill one concrete sentence under each before acting.
sourceAnchorsNote: source contains no named anecdote for this chapter

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: prevents the timestamp+named-protagonist template from dominating the chapter

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm - a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following 'concrete anchor -> abstract rule -> elaboration'
